rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 🏛️ 7 Wonders Architects — Overview 1.1 📜 Overview 1.2 🃏 Cards 1.3 ⚔️ 2-Player Battles 1.3.1 📌 Scoring examples: 1.4 ✨ Special Effects 1.5 🏁 End of Game 🏛️ 7 Wonders Architects — Overview 📜 Overview The game plays over several turns. On your turn, choose one card from the deck to your left, the deck to your right, or the middle deck (above you). Cards represent resources, science symbols, victory points, or military shields. The game ends as soon as one player's Wonder is entirely constructed. The person with the most victory points at the end wins. 🃏 Cards Resource cards (grey/yellow): Grey provide resources to construct Wonder levels. Yellow represent coins that act as wild resources. Numbers on levels show how many resources you need; icons show if they must match or differ. Science cards (green): There are 3 different science symbols. Collect 2 identical symbols or 1 of each to take a Progress Token. Victory point cards (blue): Worth 2 or 3 points. The 2-point cards show a cat symbol, letting you claim the cat pawn. This pawn allows you to see the top card of the middle deck at the start of your turn. Shield cards (red): Provide shields and 0–2 horns. Horns trigger Conflict Tokens; when full, a battle happens at the end of that player's turn. Gain 3 points if you have more Shields than each neighbor; 0 otherwise. Discard horn Shield cards after the battle. ⚔️ 2-Player Battles Having at least 1 more Shield than the opponent earns 1 Military Victory token (3 points). If you have twice as many Shields as the opponent, you earn 2 tokens (6 points). If the opponent has 0 Shields and you have 2 or more, you also take 2 tokens (6 points). 📌 Scoring examples: 1 vs 0 → 1 token = 3 pts 2 vs 0 → 2 tokens = 6 pts 2 vs 1 → 2 tokens = 6 pts 3 vs 2 → 1 token = 3 pts 4 vs 2 → 2 tokens = 6 pts ✨ Special Effects Special effects for the seven Wonders: Special effects for the 14 Progress Tokens: 🏁 End of Game The game ends as soon as one Wonder is fully constructed. The player with the most victory points wins. Victory points come from Wonder levels, the cat pawn (2 pts), blue cards, military tokens, and progress tokens. Tie-breaker: Most Wonder levels constructed.

[Rating: 1/10] What a joke... I've only draw from the common deck, no choice, no strategy.. And I've won :)) instantly sold the game :)

[Rating: 1/10] :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  One of the worst games I've played from 2021. Limited choices, significant arbitrariness, and obvious decisions. It's actually worse than OG 7 Wonders.

[Rating: 1/10] Take the best top card showing or draw a random card from the top. And $40 for trays that could've been baggies. There are way better family games than this

[Rating: 1/10] Stripped down gateway to a gateway game?  + Should be easy to teach as there is nothing here – Removed drafting the best thing about 7Wonders – Lots of random card draw x Very few decisions

[Rating: 1/10] Very mediocre gameplay Cards are completely random Players have almost no decisions This game is only hyped because of the 7 Wonders franchise Stay away!

[Rating: 1/10] Blah ugh puke. Forgettable crap, in my opinion. They took everything interesting out of 7 wonders and still dare to charge 40 bucks for it!

[Rating: 1/10] Just in case I thought 7 wonders simpliciter and duel didn't have many decisions.  At least in those you have SOME information to plan ahead on.  This is barely one step up from: randomly draw cards, determine winner.  It's not even like all cards can be variable quality depending on use or something.  It's literally, did you draw a card and leave a wild for your opponent?  That was dumb...

[Rating: 1/10] "Played" it on BGA. I don't know if "play" is a good word for this activity. It is just pulling cards and if you have luck (more than opponent(s)) then you win. You can pull all by random and still win. Or you can almost win and then have a bad luck for couple of turns and lose.   I am happy that I didn't bought this.

[Rating: 1/10] Maybe a good introductory game to play with your kids or friends who were not hardcore board gamers? [i]Maybe?[/i] But the decision space is depressingly small and the randomness of the cards that come up mean that you'll often be at the mercy of the deck. Your "best option" on any given turn is fairly obvious, so what thinking is there to do?

[Rating: 1/10] This... is not a game. There is no "play".  There are no decisions to be made. There is only the act of blindly drawing random cards and seeing whether or not you progress.  I say this with no hyperbole: Architects is Candyland without a board.
